# isArray

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is an array.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isArray() — Checks whether a value is an array. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.4.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isArray<T>(value: unknown): value is T[];
```

`Array.isArray` is the whole test, so an array from another frame counts and an array-like object — `arguments`, a `NodeList`, `{ length: 0 }` — does not.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is an array; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T[]` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isArray([]); // => true
isArray([1, 2, 3]); // => true
isArray("abc"); // => false
isArray({ length: 0 }); // => false
isArray(null); // => false
```
